## Closing evidence — all 16 acceptance criteria verified

The remedy landed as Gerrit change **3019**, commit
`8e7213f211688b9009ed25818c4ccd10ae92adb6`, carrying this ticket's
`rebar-ticket: 3083-ada3-3a0f-4051` trailer. The change took `LLM-Review +1`
and `Verified +1` and was submitted revision-scoped against that exact SHA. It
touches two files: `infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py` and
`tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py`.

### Filter and grouping criteria — read directly from the merged tree

`BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES` is defined at `handler.py:102` and contains all five
required service values verbatim: `Amazon Bedrock`,
`Claude Sonnet 4.5 (Amazon Bedrock Edition)`,
`Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Amazon Bedrock Edition)`,
`Claude Haiku 4.5 (Amazon Bedrock Edition)`, and
`Claude Opus 4.7 (Amazon Bedrock Edition)`.

It is referenced at exactly two call sites, and both are the CE `SERVICE`
dimension filter the criteria name:

| line | enclosing function | construct |
|---|---|---|
| 242 | `_refresh_rates()` (def at 234) | `"Filter": {"Dimensions": {"Key": "SERVICE", "Values": BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES}}` |
| 464 | `_ce_spend_today()` (def at 459) | same |

`_refresh_rates()` groups by both dimensions at `handler.py:243-246`:

```
"GroupBy": [
    {"Type": "DIMENSION", "Key": "SERVICE"},
    {"Type": "DIMENSION", "Key": "USAGE_TYPE"},
],
```

The label reduction and suffix mapping are `BEDROCK_EDITION_SUFFIX`
(`handler.py:109`) and `MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES` (`handler.py:110`), applied
at lines 198, 208, and 211 — `service.removesuffix(BEDROCK_EDITION_SUFFIX)`
reduces the Bedrock Edition service name to the bare model label, and
`MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES.get(token_kind)` maps `InputTokenCount` to
`input-tokens`.

### Behavioural criteria — each has a named covering test

The key shape, the per-1,000-token rate arithmetic, the `_rate_for()`
resolution, and the preservation of legacy non-Claude `Amazon Bedrock` rows are
behavioural, so they are pinned by tests rather than by reading constants:

| criterion | covering test |
|---|---|
| grouped-by-service CE query | `test_refresh_rates_queries_all_bedrock_services_grouped_by_service` |
| key shape + legacy preservation | `test_refresh_rates_bridges_claude_marketplace_and_preserves_legacy_bedrock` |
| per-1,000-token rate arithmetic | `test_refresh_rates_converts_marketplace_raw_tokens_to_thousand_token_units` |
| `_rate_for()` on the Sonnet 4.5 model id | `test_rate_for_claude_sonnet_45_uses_marketplace_empirical_rate` |
| malformed / unknown usage types | `test_marketplace_rate_key_skips_malformed_or_unknown_usage_types` |
| `_ce_spend_today()` service breadth | `test_ce_spend_today_queries_all_bedrock_services` |

### Test-run criteria

`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py`
run against the merged tree exits 0: **76 passed in 27.83s**.

The `make verify` criterion is satisfied by CI rather than locally. This host is
macOS-arm64, where 17 pandoc-backed tests fail with `Bad CPU type in executable`
for reasons unrelated to any change — so `make verify` cannot exit 0 here for
environmental reasons. The `Verified +1` on revision `8e7213f21168` is the
Linux full-suite run of exactly this contract
(`not integration and not external` on `ubuntu-latest, py3.13`), and it passed.

### Root cause, restated

The spend cap filtered Cost Explorer on the single service value
`Amazon Bedrock`. AWS bills the Claude models through separate Marketplace
services named `Claude <model> (Amazon Bedrock Edition)`, so the primary model
family produced no CE rows at all. Empirical rate discovery found nothing for
those models and silently fell back to the seed estimate, and both the warning
and the cap threshold then fired against that synthetic number rather than
against real spend. Broadening the filter to the Marketplace service values and
bridging their usage-type rows into the existing rate-key shape makes the
observed spend real.
